# Intake Brief: Main Street — Action Banking

## Problem statement

Main Street's action economy (CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R) gives players `actionsRemaining` actions each day, but every unused action is lost at day end. Players have no incentive to conserve actions for a later, bigger decision. Action banking lets unused actions accumulate across days (capped at 2 banked), enabling multi-day planning.

## Users

- **Players** of Main Street — they can now save actions across days to set up a bigger play (e.g., bank two actions then execute a move-to-hand + buy-and-place combo, or afford a premium play), turning "waste or use" into a strategic reserve.
- **TCE developers / producers** — need the banking mechanic enforced consistently in state, engine, commands, save/load, and UI so it is testable and does not regress the existing action economy.

Example user stories:
- "As a player, I want to end a quiet day without acting and start the next day with my saved action so I can plan a two-action combo."
- "As a player, I want a simple counter telling me how many actions I have banked so I know my reserve at a glance."
- "As a player with a General Manager employed, I want my extra GM action spent first so I can still bank my base action when I don't use it all."

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Banking on end-of-turn:** When the player ends a day (End Turn), every unspent action in the day's budget banks into a `bankedActions` counter (bounded by the cap). Actions bank whether zero, some, or nearly-all actions were taken (e.g., 3 available, 1 taken → 2 banked).
- 2. **Cap enforced:** `bankedActions` never exceeds 2 — further accumulation is discarded; the bank cannot grow past the cap.
- 3. **Day-start composition:** At DayStart, the day's budget is `1 base + staff actionsPerTurn bonus + bankedActions (capped 2)`. Banked reserves are consumed as the player spends actions during the day (spending draws down the combined budget).
- 4. **Staff actions used first:** Staff-derived actions (e.g., General Manager's +1 `actionsPerTurn`) are consumed before the base/banked pool; staff bonuses themselves never bank.
- 5. **UI indicator + tooltip:** HUD shows a simple banked-action count; the action tooltip explains "1 action per turn, with up to two turns' unused actions banked", including the General Manager +1 note when a GM is employed.
- 6. **State + persistence:** `bankedActions` round-trips through save/load (legacy saves default to 0), and is included in undo/redo command snapshot/restore (pattern mirroring `actionsRemaining`).
- 7. **Quality gates:** Unit tests cover banking accumulation, cap enforcement, staff-first ordering, day-start composition, save/load round-trip, and undo/redo; `npm test` passes and `npm run build` succeeds; related docs updated.

## Constraints

- **Main Street only** — no core-engine changes.
- **Bank cap fixed at 2** per operator decision (the initial seed context said 4; superseded). Max budget on any day = 1 base + staff bonus + 2 banked.
- Bank resets to 0 at new game; banked actions never expire except through spending.
- Tutorial coverage is a **separate follow-up item** (CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P) — out of scope here.
- Banking-aware AI strategy (deliberate hoarding) is a **separate follow-up item** (CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W) — out of scope here. In-scope AI behavior is passive: the AI consumes whatever budget it is given; banking accrues only when the AI happens to end a day with leftovers.
- Scope-creep guard: rebalancing the action economy, changing the cap, or redesigning the HUD layout are out of scope; record as discussion, not implementation.

## Existing state

- `state.actionsRemaining` is reset to `1 + gmBonus` at every DayStart in `executeDayStart` (MainStreetEngine.ts:851); every action-type command decrements it and throws when it is ≤ 0 (MainStreetEngine.ts:257-274, MainStreetCommands.ts:35-38).
- `actionsRemaining` is serialized/deserialized in MainStreetState.ts (line ~827) with a legacy backfill default of 1 (line ~981-983) and is part of the undo/redo command snapshot in MainStreetCommands.ts (line ~52/84/103).
- General Manager (`staff-general-manager`) grants `actionsPerTurn: 1` via the `actionsPerTurn` staff ability (shipped with CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R).
- The HUD action counter and tooltips live in `MainStreetRenderer.ts` / `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`; tutorial copy in `TutorialFlow.ts` / `TutorialScenario.ts`.

## Desired change

Add a `bankedActions` field to Main Street state, computed at day end from unspent budget (capped at 2, staff-first consumption), composed into the day-start budget, surfaced in the HUD counter and tooltip, and persisted through save/load and undo/redo. Tutorial and banking-aware AI behavior are tracked as separate follow-up items.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — add `bankedActions: number` (init 0), serialization + legacy backfill default 0 (mirror `actionsRemaining` at ~line 981).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — compute banking at day end; compose `bankedActions` into `executeDayStart` budget (currently `actionsRemaining = 1 + gmBonus` at ~line 851).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — include `bankedActions` in undo/redo snapshot/restore (pattern at ~line 52/84/103).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — serialize/deserialize `bankedActions`.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` / `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — simple banked count + explanatory tooltip (GM-aware text).
- Tests: `tests/main-street/action-banking.test.ts` (new) covering accumulation, cap, staff-first, day-start composition, save/load, undo/redo.
- Docs: `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (turn structure / action economy section).

## Related work

- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R** (done) — the base action economy this extends (`actionsRemaining`, staff actionsPerTurn, GM card).
- **CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2** (done) — single-row market + 3-slot hand defining the action list (move-to-hand, play-from-hand, buy-and-place, hire) that banking applies to.
- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** (new, follow-up) — tutorial coverage for action banking; depends on this item.
- **CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W** (new, follow-up) — banking-aware AI strategy; depends on this item.
- **CG-0MT2473NR003JEB2 / CG-0MSX41S7I009MMZN** (done) — prior AI/Monte Carlo budget-awareness tests that must still pass if any baseline shifts.

## Risks & assumptions

- **AI/Monte Carlo baseline shift:** passive AI now has up to 3–4 actions on days following an idle day, changing simulation outcomes; re-baseline `monte-carlo-baseline.json` if the harness fails, don't silently accept drift. Deliberate hoarding is explicitly follow-up work.
- **Undo/redo of banked state:** banking is computed at day end; undo must restore the pre-banking snapshot (bank count + actionsRemaining) consistently to avoid double-banking on redo.
- **Assumption — no expiry:** banked actions persist indefinitely across days (until spent), which is the simple reading of "banked". Flag if expiry is intended.
- **Assumption — passive AI in scope:** in-scope AI just consumes what it is given; this is documented here and in the AI follow-up item so expectations are explicit.
- **Scope-creep risk:** redesigning how staff vs base actions are displayed, changing the cap, or adding bank spend-splitting rules are out of scope; record as linked work, don't implement here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (scope): "Is this banking mechanic specific to Main Street, or a core-engine feature?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "Main Street." Source: interactive reply. Accepted: Main Street only; no core-engine changes.
- Q2 (cap & composition): "Cap is 4 in the seed — is that right? Is the cap a separate bank counter or does it bound total actions?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "Make the bank cap 2, not 4 and it is banked + base 1." Source: interactive reply. Accepted: cap 2 banked; day budget = banked (≤2) + base 1 (+ staff bonus).
- Q3 (bank trigger): "When do actions bank — only on explicit End-Turn without acting, or also when skipping?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "ends turn without taking an action." Source: interactive reply. Refined by Q4 (partial use) to mean "at end of turn, from whatever remains".
- Q4 (partial use): "If a turn has 3 actions available and the player takes only 1, do the unused ones bank?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "any left over actions can be banked, so in your example the remaining 2 are banked." Source: interactive reply. Accepted: banking is on unspent remainder at end of day (not only when nothing was taken).
- Q5 (staff-first): "Does an unused GM action bank? Does the GM +1 change the max?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "no, only the players base actions bank. Staff actions are used first." Source: interactive reply. Accepted: staff-derived actions are consumed first and never bank; only base-portion remains bankable. Net effect: with GM, an idle day banks only the base 1.
- Q6 (cap-at-cap): "If the bank is already at the cap and the player ends a turn with no action, what happens?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "yes" (bank stays at 2; overflow discarded). Source: interactive reply.
- Q7 (UI): "How should banked actions be shown?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "just a simple count is fine (add a tooltip that explains 1 action per turn with up to two unused turns banked). # Evaluate and balance synergy-type distribution across Main Street tiers

**Type:** Task | **Priority:** High | **Assignee:** Map

## Problem Statement

Synergy types (the "business types" / synergs that drive adjacency bonuses) are distributed unevenly across Main Street's 12 progression tiers. Source of truth is `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` (`tier` column 1–12, `synergyTypes` column, `|`-separated). Only business (30) and community-space (8) cards carry synergy types; events, upgrades, and staff carry none.

Per-tier synergy-bearing card counts and type assignments today:

| Tier | cards w/ synergy | assignments | type distribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | 6 | 6 | Culture 3, Food 2, Service 1 |
| T2 | 3 | 3 | Commerce 3 |
| T3 | 2 | 2 | Entertainment 2 |
| T4 | 4 | 4 | Entertainment 1, Food 2, Service 1 |
| T5 | 5 | 6 | Commerce 1, Culture 2, Entertainment 1, Food 1, Health 1 |
| T6 | 3 | 3 | Commerce 1, Service 2 |
| T7 | 3 | 4 | Culture 2, Food 2 |
| T8 | 4 | 4 | Culture 1, Food 1, Health 2 |
| T9 | 2 | 3 | Culture 1, Health 2 |
| T10 | 2 | 2 | Entertainment 1, Health 1 |
| T11 | 3 | 5 | Entertainment 1, Health 2, Service 2 |
| T12 | 4 | 6 | Culture 2, Entertainment 2, Health 1, Service 1 |

Global type totals (lopsided): Commerce 5, Culture 11, Food 8, Service 7, Entertainment 8, Health 9.

Under the target rule "no type exceeds 2× another within a tier", **T1 (3 vs 1), T2 (3 vs 0), T3 (2 vs 0) fail today**; the rest pass.

## Goal

Analyse the per-tier synergy-type distribution, then adjust `card-data.csv` so every tier has an even, balanced spread — no synergy type's count within a tier exceeds 2× any other type's count in that tier (and each tier spans ≥2 distinct types). The change mirrors the completed family-balance rebalance (CG-0MT2WU0CX005Z143), but along the synergy-type axis.

## Users

- **Players** — a tier's unlock shouldn't railroad good synergy builds into one family; each tier should offer comparable synergy variety.
- **Designers/balance** — predictable, documented per-tier synergy composition for future expansion.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Analysis output:** The work item publishes the before-snapshot per-tier distribution (counts per type, max/min ratio per tier) with failing tiers identified, and the after-snapshot showing the rule now holds — surfaced in the work item description/comment and/or `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`.
2. **Balanced spread:** After CSV adjustments, for every tier 1–12 with synergy-bearing cards: min type count ≥ 1 and max type count ≤ 2× min type count (i.e. ≥2 distinct types per tier, no type dominating at >2×).
3. **Constraint levers, in order of preference:** (a) retag existing synergy-bearing business/community cards only where the new type fits the card's flavour ("retagging is acceptable where it makes sense for the card type"); (b) introduce/relocate **bridge cards** (dual-type cards) into sparse tiers — a bridge counts one card toward two types, efficient where a tier has only 2–3 synergy-bearing slots; (c) add new cards when (a)/(b) cannot reach balance.
4. **No synergy types added to cards that currently have none** (events/upgrades/staff/untagged community spaces remain synergy-free).
5. **Flavour preserved:** designed synergy pairings survive (e.g. Bookshop↔Library culture pairing CG-0MSKS963N, Food|Culture bridges Cafe/Teahouse); retags must match card identity.
6. **Tests:** new `tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` (pattern: `tier-family-balance.test.ts`) asserts the ≤2× rule + ≥2 types per tier; existing tier-composition/manifest/catalog tests updated for any moved/added cards.
7. **Docs updated:** main-street docs (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`) reflect the synergy-balance model.
8. **Quality gates:** `npm test` (full suite) and `npm run build` pass.

## Constraints

- No `synergyTypes` added to cards currently without them (user directive).
- Retagging allowed where flavour-sensible.
- New cards allowed, but additions stay minimal (cost ladder and tier economy still apply).
- Seeded determinism: deck-composition changes shift seeded RNG draws deliberately; document per precedent CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R.
- Independent of in-progress staff-market item CG-0MT2WTN0L004JA53 (staff have no synergy types; disjoint dimension, no blocking).

## Existing state

See Problem Statement tables. Bridge cards (dual-type) already exist: Food Truck (Food|Ent, T4), Florist (Commerce|Culture, T5), Juice Bar (Food|Health, T5), Teahouse (Food|Culture, T7), Cafe (Food|Culture, T8), Yoga Studio (Culture|Health, T9), Day Spa (Service|Ent, T11), Physiotherapy (Health|Service, T11), Art Gallery (Culture|Ent, T12), Public Art (Culture|Ent, T12). **T1, T2, T3, T6, T10 have no bridges** — the sparse tiers that need them most.

## Desired change

1. Produce and commit the per-tier synergy distribution analysis (before/after).
2. Retag/relocate/add cards so every tier satisfies the ≤2× rule, using bridges to stretch sparse tiers (e.g. a 2-card tier can span 3–4 types via one dual-type bridge).
3. Guard the result with the new balance test; keep flavour pairings intact.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — synergyTypes/tier reassignments (primary change surface).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — CARD_TIER_MAP plumbing; no structural change expected.
- `tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` — **new**, mirroring `tier-family-balance.test.ts`.
- `tests/main-street/tier-catalog-coverage.test.ts`, `meta-progression.test.ts`, `card-manifest.test.ts`, `card-catalog-baseline.test.ts` — update as needed.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — doc updates.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT2WU0CX005Z143** (completed) — Rebalance card families across progression tiers; same pattern along the family axis; `tier-family-balance.test.ts` precedent.
- **CG-0MT3C744B009DS84** (completed) — 5→12 tier expansion; current 12-tier structure.
- **CG-0MSQJ1XIB0004QVN** (completed) — Group A: business synergy depth & bridges (origin of bridge cards).
- **CG-0MSKS963N** (completed) — Library next to Bookshop synergy pairing (flavour constraint).
- **CG-0MS9HJ8SU008MJQQ** (completed) — CSV: rebalance Library & repurpose Community Hub (retagging precedent).
- **CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE** (completed) — culture/library income flavour rationale (guard against flavour-blind retags).
- **CG-0MSQJ210I00491ZZ / CG-0MSQE2NLX003ADIY / CG-0MSQJ1XIB0004QVN** (completed) — basis of the current card pool (business bridges, community-space expansion, 50+ card design).
- **CG-0MSP1HCAS00785MP / CG-0MSP263PL006GRSK / CG-0MSX2PI7X002014B** (completed) — 8-way adjacency synergy + tests (must keep passing).
- **CG-0MT2WTN0L004JA53** (in-progress) — staff market removal; same CSV, disjoint dimension.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Flavour binds flexibility:** if retags/bridges can't reach balance for a tier without violating card identity, new cards are needed — treat additions as minimal scope; any larger pool expansions become separate work items (scope-creep guard).
- **Assumption — per-tier balance, not global totals:** "even spread" is defined per tier (≤2× rule, user-stated); globally lopsided type totals (Commerce 5 vs Culture 11) are tolerated unless explicitly resurfaced.
- **Assumption — count basis:** the ≤2× rule applies to synergy-type assignment counts (bridge cards count once per type they carry), consistent with the analysis tables above.
- **Seeded RNG shifts:** any deck-size change alters seeded draws; accepted and documented (precedent CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R).
- **No blocking dependency** on CG-0MT2WTN0L004JA53, but CSV conflicts possible if both edit `card-data.csv` concurrently — coordinate via worktrees/rebasing.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope: analysis-only, analysis + CSV reassignments, or also a regression check/test?" — Answer (rgardler): **(b) analysis + actual card-data.csv reassignments** to achieve the even spread. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "What does even spread mean — coverage of all 6 types per tier, balanced counts with tolerance, or progressive introduction?" — Answer (rgardler): **(b) balanced counts, no type >2× another within a tier.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "May we add synergyTypes to cards that currently have none? Are retags OK? How do bridge cards fit? May we add new cards?" — Answer (rgardler): **"Do not add to existing cards. Retagging is acceptable where it makes sense for the card type. How would bridge cards come into play here? You can also add new cards if necessary."** Research: 10 existing dual-type bridge cards concentrated in T4/5/7/8/9/11/12; none in the sparse tiers T1/T2/T3/T6/T10. Bridge answer: a bridge counts a single card toward two synergy types, so sparse tiers (2–3 synergy-bearing cards) can span 3–4 types with one dual card; relocating existing flavour-sensible bridges or adding new ones to sparse tiers is the primary lever combined with retagging.

# Upgrade cards: consume an action and go to hand first (drag-drop = buy & play same turn)

## Plan Changelog

**2026-08-22**: Plan created (7 child work items, test-first ordering, Medium effort/Medium risk).

## Plan Summary

This work item decomposes the upgrade economy fix into 7 child tasks with test-first ordering:

### Phase 1: Unit Tests (test-first, no dependencies)
- **CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9** — Unit tests: upgrade action economy

### Phase 2: Core Engine Wiring (parallel with browser tests)
- **CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT** — Engine: wire action cost into upgrade commands

### Phase 3: Implementation (3 parallel tracks)
- **CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D** — Engine: implement hand-first click flow + target selection
- **CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7** — Engine: implement drag-drop buy-and-play
- **CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q** — AI and Monte Carlo: budget-aware upgrade actions

### Browser Tests (test-first, parallel with implementation)
- **CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC** — Browser tests: hand-first click flow for upgrades
- **CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1** — Browser tests: drag-drop and premium for upgrades

### Phase 4: Integration & Polish
- **CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK** — Update existing tests, E2E, and documentation

### Dependency Graph
```
CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9 (unit tests)
       |
       v
CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT (engine: action cost)
    /      |       \
   v       v        v
CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D  CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7  CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q
(hand-first flow)    (drag-drop)           (AI/MC)
       \                |                /
        \               |               /
         v              v              v
        CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK (update tests/E2E/docs)

CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC (browser: hand flow) ---\
CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1 (browser: drag-drop) ----/
       |
       +-- blocks respective implementation children
```

## Problem statement

Playing an upgrade card currently costs **no action** and never passes through the hand — a market upgrade click applies the upgrade directly to the first eligible business (`buyUpgradeCommand` → `purchaseUpgrade`, no `consumeAction()`). This diverges from the business-card economy (move-to-hand = 1 action, same-day place free, held-card play = 1 action, drag-drop buy-and-place = 1 action + 50% premium) and gives upgrade cards a free second daily action. Upgrades should behave like business cards: go to the hand first when bought by click, with drag-and-drop as the same-turn buy-and-play path.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want playing an upgrade card to consume one of my daily actions like every other purchase/play **so that** the action economy stays honest (1 action/day, 2 with General Manager) and upgrades aren't a free lunch.
- **As a player**, I want upgrades I buy to land in my hand first **so that** I can choose when and where to apply them (target a specific business, possibly next day).
- **As a player**, I want to drag an upgrade straight from the market onto a business when I'm sure **so that** I can buy-and-play in one turn at a +50% premium, exactly like business buy-and-place.
- **As a player**, I want to pick which business to upgrade when playing from hand **so that** I can respond to my current street layout (e.g. branches / multi-level chains).

## Acceptance Criteria (Parent)

- [ ] **Action cost — click path:** Clicking a market upgrade moves it to hand and consumes 1 action; playing the same-day moved upgrade applies it with no additional action; playing a held-from-previous-day upgrade consumes 1 action. All paths decrement actionsRemaining and legality gates reject the action when the budget is spent.
- [ ] **Hand-first + target selection:** Upgrade market cards follow the two-step hand flow — never applied directly from the market on click. When an upgrade is selected in hand, the player clicks an eligible business on the street to apply it; ineligible targets are rejected with illegal-move feedback.
- [ ] **Drag-drop same-turn:** Upgrades in the market are draggable onto eligible street businesses — drag-drop = buy & play in the same turn, consumes 1 action, and charges the +50% premium. Illegal drops snap back with feedback.
- [ ] **Free ops unchanged:** Event cards' free move-to-hand and free play stay free; refresh, sell, hint, discard, community favour, end-turn remain non-action operations.
- [ ] **AI + Monte Carlo:** MainStreetAiStrategy and MainStreetMonteCarlo account for the upgrade action cost in budget-aware valuation, and remain deterministic per seed.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** New unit tests cover action spend + gating for all three upgrade paths; browser tests cover the hand-first click flow, drag-drop onto eligible/illegal targets, and action-budget dimming; existing upgrade tests updated to the new flow.
- [ ] **Docs:** All related documentation updated; full project test suite (npm test) and npm run build pass.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing action economy: 1 action/day (2 with General Manager) — upgrades must not create a second implicitly-free action.
- Same-day composite stays free (consistency with business cards); the 50% premium formula must match the business buy-and-place exactly.
- Undo/redo must wrap the new paths (snapshotted commands; new actions after undo invalidate the redo stack).
- State/transcript/save-load fields must stay consistent (e.g. justMovedHandCardId semantics generalise to upgrades; pendingUpgradeIndex-style state added if needed).
- Reduced-motion and mute settings must be respected by any new animation/SFX.

## Effort and Risk

- **Effort:** Medium (37.83h recommended, range [26h-57h])
- **Risk:** Medium (score 10/25, confidence 74%)

# Intake Brief: Quarter the reputation-based income coin multiplier (CG-0MT3J80HV0084IF1)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Feature** | **Assignee: Map**

> Reduce the reputation→income coin multiplier to a quarter of its current strength: `reputationCoinDivisor` 20 → 80 and `maxReputationCoinMultiplier` 3.0 → 1.5 in all three presets (Easy/Medium/Hard). Formula shape unchanged: `multiplier = min(1 + rep/divisor, cap)`.

## Problem Statement

The reputation-based income coin multiplier scales income too aggressively. With divisor=20, reputation=20 **doubles** income (2.0×) and reputation=40 **triples** it (3.0× cap) — making direct business income secondary to reputation snowball in longer games. Operator directive: *"The income multiplier from reputation is too high, quarter it."* — quarter the additive bonus above the 1.0× baseline (divisor 20→80) and scale the cap's additive portion by the same factor (2.0 → 0.5, i.e. cap 3.0 → 1.5).

## Users

- **Player** — wants income to stay primarily driven by the businesses they build; reputation should be a modest bonus, not the dominant income engine.
  - *"As a player, I want reputation to boost my income a quarter as strongly so that building good businesses remains the main income strategy."*
- **Producer / balancer** — wants a minimal, test-covered retune that preserves the multiplier's formula shape, its cap behavior (still bites at rep=40), and the preset invariants.
  - *"As a balancer, I want the retune expressed purely via preset constants so the model stays uniform across difficulties."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Formula shape unchanged (`min(1 + rep/divisor, cap)`); preset values updated in `EASY_PRESET`, `MEDIUM_PRESET`, and `HARD_PRESET`: `reputationCoinDivisor` **20 → 80**, `maxReputationCoinMultiplier` **3.0 → 1.5**.
2. Multiplier reference points: rep=0 → 1.0×; rep=10 → **1.125×** (was 1.5×); rep=20 → **1.25×** (was 2.0×); rep=40 → **1.5×** — cap now bites at rep=40 (was 3.0×); rep≥40 → capped 1.5×.
3. Behavior invariants preserved: negative/zero reputation → 1.0× baseline; zero/negative coin deltas pass through unscaled; fractional income preserved (no `Math.floor` — CG-0MRER3RE300418SG).
4. All affected tests updated and passing: `tests/main-street/reputation-coin-multiplier.test.ts` (DEFAULT_CFG, reference points, preset sanity — Medium start rep=3 → 1.0375, Easy rep=5 → 1.0625, Hard rep=2 → 1.025), `tests/main-street/hud-tooltips.test.ts` (rep=20 → ×1.25; cap display ×1.5), `tests/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.test.ts` rep-multiplier parity, and every Main Street income/event test asserting coin totals under default config (rep=3: multiplier 1.15 → 1.0375). New regression points pin the quartered values (rep=20 → 1.25×, cap 1.5×).
5. Code comments/JSDoc and docs updated wherever the multiplier formula/values are described (`MainStreetDifficulty.ts` JSDoc reference-point examples; any relevant docs prose). Explicitly **out of scope**: `reputationScoreMultiplier` (final-score rep×5), and the `rep-multiplier` / `income-multiplier` ActiveEffect values.
6. Full project test suite passes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` succeeds.

## Constraints

- Formula shape must not change — quartering is expressed solely via the preset constants `reputationCoinDivisor` and `maxReputationCoinMultiplier`.
- Applies identically to all three difficulty presets (they currently share 20 / 3.0).
- Do **not** touch `reputationScoreMultiplier` (5.0, used in `finalScore = coins + rep*5 + ...`) — that is the *score* multiplier, not the income multiplier.
- Monte Carlo re-baselining (`avgCoinsPerTurn`, `winRate` targets in the balance harness) is **not** part of this item unless explicitly requested — see Risks.

## Existing State

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — `reputationCoinMultiplier()` = `min(1 + rep/reputationCoinDivisor, maxReputationCoinMultiplier)`; all presets 20 / 3.0. Current: rep=10 → 1.5×, rep=20 → 2.0×, rep=40 → 3.0× (cap).
- `applyReputationMultiplier()` scales only positive coin deltas (income + positive events); penalties pass through unchanged.
- Consumers: `MainStreetEngine.ts` (income/event resolution), `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` (`applyIncome`); HUD tooltips render the multiplier dynamically (no UI code change expected — `hud-tooltips.test.ts` only).
- Tests asserting multiplier values: `reputation-coin-multiplier.test.ts`, `hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `EconomyLedger.test.ts` (parity), plus ~15 Main Street income/event test files whose coin-total expectations shift under default rep=3 (1.15× → 1.0375×).

## Desired Change

1. In `MainStreetDifficulty.ts`: set `reputationCoinDivisor: 80` and `maxReputationCoinMultiplier: 1.5` in `EASY_PRESET`, `MEDIUM_PRESET`, `HARD_PRESET`; update `reputationCoinMultiplier()` JSDoc reference-point examples.
2. Update the affected test expectations (reference points, preset sanity, tooltip display, EconomyLedger parity, and income/event coin totals under default config); add regression pins for the quartered values.
3. Review/update docs prose that describes the multiplier where values are stated.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — **edit** — preset constants (divisor 80, cap 1.5) + JSDoc examples
- `tests/main-street/reputation-coin-multiplier.test.ts` — **edit** — DEFAULT_CFG + all reference-point/preset assertions
- `tests/main-street/hud-tooltips.test.ts` — **edit** — multiplier display expectations (×1.25, cap ×1.5)
- `tests/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.test.ts` — **edit** — rep-multiplier integration parity values
- ~15 income/event test files under `tests/main-street/` — **edit** — coin-total expectations under default rep=3 (see context-gathering list: activity-log, adjacency, clinic-health-synergy, duration-event-resolution, graffiti-art-incident, group-c/d/f expansions, income-decay, incremental-income, MainStreetHandSynergy, MainStreetIntegration, reputation-coin-multiplier, turnflow, income-collection.browser)
- `docs/rule-engine/economy-ledger.md`, `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — **review** — multiplier prose; update only where values are stated

## Related Work

- **CG-0MSP26Q5N002EH8P** [completed] — Monte Carlo baseline and balance re-tune. Precedent for how balance retunes are validated (issueType feature, priority high; Monte Carlo re-baseline).
- **CG-0MRER3RE300418SG** [completed] — Removed `Math.floor` from `applyReputationMultiplier`; fractional-income expectations this item must preserve.
- **CG-0MMLR38NJ1N11DOS** — original reputation-based coin multiplier work (tests' header reference).
- **CG-0MSRKN325004ELH2** [completed] — Review optimal pass values for `avgCoinsPerTurn`, `winRate`, `medianScore` (Monte Carlo targets this retune will shift).

### Related work (automated report)

Generated by `/skill:find-related CG-0MT3J80HV0084IF1`:

- **CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ** [blocked] — Income Phase: phased card-effect animations (coin grids, synergy/rep/event contributions). Shares the income/rep contribution path this retune touches; its phased-animation presentation will need to reflect the new values.
- **CG-0MSKT0NQP0018KK6** [completed] — Core-engine drag-drop module with unit tests. (Low direct relevance; matched shared terms.)
- **CG-0MSXNRO8S001DSWJ** [completed] — Fix dev-server OOM root cause in transcript plugin. (Low direct relevance.)

Repository file matches were the draft/balance docs only (no code path outside MainStreetDifficulty/tests references the multiplier constants).

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

- **Test blast radius:** every Main Street income/event coin assertion under default config shifts (rep=3: 1.15× → 1.0375×). Mitigation: update expectations deliberately per-assertion rather than bulk-regenerating, to preserve test intent; run the full unit project.
- **Monte Carlo baselines drift:** `avgCoinsPerTurn` drops; `winRate`/`medianScore` targets in the balance harness are no longer calibrated. Mitigation: record a follow-up re-baseline work item instead of expanding this item's scope.
- **Scope creep:** `reputationScoreMultiplier`, `rep-multiplier`/`income-multiplier` ActiveEffect values, Community Favour costs, and card `reputationPerTurn` are separate balance levers — record as linked follow-ups if requested, do not fold in.
- **Dead/unreachable config avoided deliberately:** the cap is scaled 3.0 → 1.5 (not left at 3.0) so it still bites at rep=40 with the new divisor — quartering stays internally consistent.

### Assumptions

- "Quarter it" = divide the additive bonus above the 1.0× baseline by 4 (equivalently divisor 20 → 80) **and** scale the cap's additive portion 2.0 → 0.5 (cap 1.5) — confirmed by the operator during intake (Q1, Q2).
- All three presets are tuned identically (they share 20 / 3.0 today).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

1. **Q: What does "quarter it" mean for the formula?** (Proposed: quarter the additive bonus above the 1.0× baseline — `multiplier = 1 + rep/80`, i.e. divisor 20 → 80 — so rep=20 drops 2.0× → 1.25×. Alternatives: quarter the whole multiplier, which drops below baseline and penalizes income; or something else.)
   — **A (user): "1. go with your proposal"** — divisor 20 → 80 (quarter the additive bonus). Source: interactive reply.
2. **Q: What is the cap, and how is it applied?** — A (agent, informational): `maxReputationCoinMultiplier` is a per-preset config value; `reputationCoinMultiplier()` returns `min(1 + rep/divisor, cap)`; `applyReputationMultiplier()` multiplies only positive coin deltas. With divisor=20 the 3.0 cap bites at rep=40 and prevents runaway scaling (rep=60 would otherwise be 4.0×). After the divisor change, cap 3.0 would need rep=160 (no-op), so re-scaling is required.
3. **Q: What happens to the 3.0× cap?** Options: (a) cap → 1.5 (scale the bonus portion 2.0 → 0.5; keeps cap biting at rep=40), (b) leave at 3.0 (becomes dead config in practice), (c) remove the cap (reintroduces snowball).
   — **A (user): "2. a"** — cap 3.0 → 1.5. Source: interactive reply.

### Plan: changelog (2026-08-22)

Planning executed via /skill:plan. Created 2 child work items (test-first ordering):

1. **CG-0MT4ARX4500316RM** — Update reputation-based income multiplier presets, JSDoc, and all affected tests (task, high)
2. **CG-0MT4ASE64003CBEK** — Verify: full test suite and build pass after multiplier retune (task, medium)

# Feature 1: State, Serialization & Refill — Staff in the General Market

Part of **Remove dedicated staff market; route staff cards into general market selection** (CG-0MT2WTN0L004JA53).

## Problem

`MainStreetState` carries a dedicated `staffCardMarket: StaffCard[]` field populated by a separate staff deck never drawn from or cycled through the general market row. Layoff returns laid-off staff to `staffCardMarket`. Nothing routes staff through `state.market.cards` or the standard refill/cycle pipeline.

## Goal

Remove the dedicated staff-market state. Staff cards live in a tier-filtered staff deck inside the general deck pool (`decks.staff`), drawn into the single-row market by the standard refill, with `discards.staff` for the cycling/reshuffle pipeline — exactly like business/community-space/upgrade/event.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `staffCardMarket` is removed from the `MainStreetState` and `MainStreetSerializedState` interfaces (types, clone code, setup, serialization, deserialization, migration); the game no longer offers staff from a separate market section.
2. `decks.staff: StaffCard[]` and `discards.staff: StaffCard[]` exist on the state and serialized types; `setupMainStreetGame` creates the staff deck via `createStaffDeck(1, options.unlockedCardIds)` (already tier-filtered by prerequisite CG-0MT2WU0CX005Z143), shuffles it with the seeded RNG, and stores it in `state.decks.staff`.
3. `refillSingleRowMarket` draws staff cards into the market row with a new `MARKET_STAFF_MAX` composition bound (e.g. 0-1 staff per row), including `reshuffleIfNeeded`/`forceReshuffleFromDiscards` support for `discards.staff`, and returns un-drawn staff to `decks.staff`.
4. Serialize/deserialize round-trip drops `staffCardMarket` and preserves `decks.staff`/`discards.staff`.
5. Save migration: legacy saves containing `staffCardMarket` transfer those cards into `decks.staff` (preserving the cards in the game); the old `staffCardMarket = []` backfill is removed. Old saves without the field load without error.
6. Seeded determinism preserved (same seed ⇒ same game); any shuffle-order changes are deliberate and documented in the setup comment.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Edit `MainStreetState.ts`: remove `staffCardMarket` from both interfaces; add `staff` to `decks` and `discards` interfaces.
2. Update `setupMainStreetGame`: build staff deck, shuffle via seeded RNG, store in `state.decks.staff`; drop `staffCardMarket: staffDeck`.
3. Update `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState` for the new field set; update `migrateSerializedState` to fold legacy `staffCardMarket` into `decks.staff`.
4. Add `MARKET_STAFF_MAX` to the market constants; extend `refillSingleRowMarket` with a `drawStaff` path and the new composition bound.
5. Update `TutorialScenario.ts` state literal (remove `staffCardMarket: []`, add `decks.staff`/`discards.staff` as needed to satisfy the type).

## Tests

- State setup: staff deck present in `decks.staff`, tier-filtered by `unlockedCardIds`.
- Serialize/deserialize round-trip: no `staffCardMarket` in serialized form; `decks.staff`/`discards.staff` round-trip.
- Migration: legacy save with `staffCardMarket` → cards appear in `decks.staff`; legacy save without it loads cleanly.
- Refill: over many seeded refills, staff appear in the row within `MARKET_STAFF_MAX` bound; un-drawn staff return to `decks.staff`.

## Dependencies

None (foundation); prerequisite CG-0MT2WU0CX005Z143 already merged.

## Deliverables

- Updated `MainStreetState.ts`, `TutorialScenario.ts`
- Updated/new tests in `tests/main-street/`
- Documentation of the composition change in the refill comment

## Verification

Feature 2 depends on this; parent AC1, AC2, AC6.

# Feature 2: Purchase Path, Hire & AI — Unified Staff Purchase

Part of **Remove dedicated staff market; route staff cards into general market selection** (CG-0MT2WTN0L004JA53). Depends on Feature 1 (State, Serialization & Refill).

## Problem

Staff are purchased through a separate path: `purchaseStaffCard` looks up `state.staffCardMarket` and `hireStaffCard` wraps it, while the general market's cycle/refill logic (business/community-space/upgrade/event family routing) and `moveToHand` know nothing about staff. The AI never generates `hire-staff` actions (`enumerateLegalActions` has no staff branch), so staff hiring is dead code from the AI's perspective.

## Goal

Staff purchases go through the normal market purchase path: legality checks against the market row, deduction + discards routing like other families, hire action resolved against `state.market.cards`, layoff returning cards to the market pipeline, and the AI able to hire staff from the general market.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `canPurchaseStaff(state, cardId)` returns a `LegalityResult` (card present, `family === 'staff'`, coins sufficient).
2. `purchaseStaffCard` operates on `state.market.cards` (finds `family === 'staff'`), deducts coins, removes the card from the market, pushes it to `state.staffCards`, increases `maxHandSize` by `handSlotsAdded`, and routes the removed card to `discards.staff`; throws meaningful errors when illegal.
3. `hireStaffCard` (engine) resolves the card in `state.market.cards` (not `staffCardMarket`), consumes one daily action, and delegates to the unified `purchaseStaffCard`; the `hire-staff` action type still works through `executeAction`.
4. `cycleMarketCards` and `refreshMarket` route `family === 'staff'` cards to `discards.staff`.
5. `moveToHand` rejects staff cards (`family === 'staff'` → illegal; staff are hired directly, never moved to hand).
6. `layoffStaffCard` returns the laid-off card to `discards.staff` (available again on the next refill/cycle) instead of `staffCardMarket`.
7. `enumerateLegalActions` generates `hire-staff` actions for affordable staff cards in the general market (not already employed), so the AI can hire; the existing `scoreAction` `hire-staff` branch is exercised.

## Minimal Implementation

1. `MainStreetMarket.ts`: rename/adapt `purchaseStaffCard` to the market row; add `canPurchaseStaff`; extend `cycleMarketCards`/`refreshMarket` discard routing with `staff`; guard `moveToHand`/`moveCardToHand` against staff.
2. `MainStreetEngine.ts`: update `hireStaffCard` lookup; change `layoffStaffCard` return target to `discards.staff`.
3. `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`: add a `hire-staff` branch to `enumerateLegalActions` (affordable staff in market, not already employed, action budget available).

## Tests

- `canPurchaseStaff` legality (found/missing card, insufficient coins, wrong family).
- `purchaseStaffCard`: coins deducted, market row updated, `staffCards` grown, `maxHandSize` increased, discard routed, refill behavior.
- `hireStaffCard` via `executeAction` consumes the daily action (regression for `action-economy` contract).
- `layoffStaffCard` → card available again via `discards.staff` (decks/discards, refill).
- `cycleMarketCards`/`refreshMarket` staff routing.
- `moveToHand` rejects staff.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes `hire-staff` for affordable staff and the greedy AI hires staff in a seeded run.

## Dependencies

Feature 1 (state/serialization/refill).

## Deliverables

- Updated `MainStreetMarket.ts`, `MainStreetEngine.ts`, `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
- Updated/new tests in `tests/main-street/`

## Verification

Parent AC2, AC4; regression for the existing `action-economy`/`refresh-market` staff contracts.

# Feature 3: UI & Interaction — Staff Render and Hire in the Market Row

Part of **Remove dedicated staff market; route staff cards into general market selection** (CG-0MT2WTN0L004JA53). Depends on Features 1-2.

## Problem

The general market row UI (`MainStreetRenderer.drawMarketRow`) dispatches card clicks by family — business/community-space → click-to-place, upgrade → upgrade click, else event → event click — and knows nothing about staff. With staff cards now flowing through `state.market.cards` (Feature 1-2), the renderer must render them in-row with a hire interaction and tooltip, and the tutorial's state literal must no longer reference `staffCardMarket`.

## Goal

Staff cards render in the market row like other cards and are purchased through a hire click that consumes one daily action — consistent with the rest of the market surface. No orphaned staff-market UI code remains.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Staff cards render in the market row (existing SVG card rendering path) indistinguishable in layout from other families.
2. Clicking a staff card in the market invokes the hire flow: `MainStreetRenderer.drawMarketRow` dispatches `family === 'staff'` to a new `onStaffCardClick` handler that performs `hireStaffCard` (consuming 1 action), with the same animated + SFX feedback path as other market actions; staff cards are not treated as move-to-hand cards.
3. Staff card tooltips show hire-relevant info (name, cost, +N hand slots, ongoing cost/turn, abilities such as refresh discount / peek / +action).
4. The `drawMarketRow` type signatures accept `StaffCard`; no orphaned `staffCardMarket` references or staff-market-specific UI code remain in `example-games/main-street/scenes/` or elsewhere.
5. Tutorial scenario loads without error (state literal updated per Feature 1; no reference to a staff market section).
6. HUD tooltips / help text that mention a separate staff market or a non-market hire surface are updated to the unified-market model.

## Minimal Implementation

1. `MainStreetRenderer.ts`: extend `drawMarketRow`/`drawMarketCard` family dispatch with `staff` → `onStaffCardClick`; ensure tooltips (buildCardTooltipInfo or staff-specific) cover staff cards.
2. `MainStreetScene.ts` + `MainStreetTurnController.ts` + `MainStreetInputManager.ts`: add `onStaffCardClick` wiring through the same action path used by other market purchases (command `rent: hireStaffCardCommand`, SFX/animation per the shared convention).
3. `TutorialScenario.ts`: confirm the tutorial needs no staff-specific market handling post-Feature 1 (staff only appear in the general row).
4. `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`: update action-consumes/tooltip text if it references a dedicated staff surface.
5. Grep sweep: no `staffCardMarket` references remain in `example-games/` or `tests/`.

## Tests

- Renderer/browser test: staff card renders in the market row and click triggers the hire flow (or scoped input-level test where browser replays are impractical).
- Interaction test: market-phase click on a staff card consumes 1 action and moves the card to active staff.
- Regression: tutorial E2E (parts affected by market composition) still green.
- Grep-based assertion (unit): no `staffCardMarket` identifier anywhere in `example-games/` or `tests/`.

## Dependencies

Features 1, 2.

## Deliverables

- Updated renderer/scene/controller/input files
- Browser or interaction tests
- Tooltip/content updates

## Verification

Parent AC4, AC5; player-visible verification via the browser suite.

# Feature 4: Test Fixes, Docs & Monte-Carlo Baseline

Part of **Remove dedicated staff market; route staff cards into general market selection** (CG-0MT2WTN0L004JA53). Depends on Features 1-3.

## Problem

~13 existing test files reference `staffCardMarket` or assume the dedicated staff market (`MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts`, `action-economy.test.ts`, `command-action-economy.test.ts`, `refresh-market.test.ts`, `MainStreetIntegration.test.ts`, `ai-action-budget.test.ts`, `meta-progression.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`, `group-a-business-expansion.test.ts`, others as grep finds them). Docs still describe the dedicated staff market (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`: staff "are purchased from the dedicated staff-card market"; `core-rules-and-mechanics.md`: "From the staff market"; `prd-multi-use-card-economy.md`: dedicated `staffCardMarket` section). The Monte-Carlo baseline (`docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`) assumes staff are never in the market row, so market composition changes will shift guardrail metrics.

## Goal

All tests pass against the unified market model, docs describe the unified market, and the Monte-Carlo baseline is regenerated to reflect staff in the market row.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All existing test files referencing the dedicated staff market are updated to the unified-market model; grep for `staffCardMarket` returns zero hits in `example-games/` and `tests/` (except migration fixtures that intentionally test legacy-save compatibility).
2. Full `npm test` passes (unit + browser + tutorial E2E stages through `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`).
3. `npm run build` succeeds (TypeScript check + Vite production build).
4. `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` staff section states staff are tier-gated and purchased from the general market row (no dedicated staff market), matching the implementation.
5. `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` actions table and `docs/main-street/prd-multi-use-card-economy.md` describe the unified market (staff drawn into the general row, hired from the market, laid-off staff return via the market pipeline).
6. `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json` regenerated from the current implementation; `monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` passes within tolerance bands; any band changes are justified in the baseline commit message.
7. Any other docs referencing the staff market (e.g. `content-design-and-progression.md`, PRDs, `example-games/main-street/README.md`) are consistent with the unified model.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Update the affected test files to build staff into the general market (setup-level helper or focusing on market rows) and assert through the unified purchase/hire path.
2. Add save/load migration test: legacy serialized state with `staffCardMarket` loads and staff flow into `decks.staff`.
3. Regenerate `monte-carlo-baseline.json` via `npm run monte-carlo` and verify guardrail tests pass.
4. Update `card-catalog.md` (staff section), `core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (actions table), `prd-multi-use-card-economy.md` (staff market references), `content-design-and-progression.md` if staff-market language appears, `example-games/main-street/README.md`.
5. Run full `npm test` and `npm run build`; triage any failures (change seeded-draw expectations only where the change is deliberate and documented per parent AC6).

## Tests

Full suite green (`npm test`), build green (`npm run build`), migration test, baseline guardrail test.

## Dependencies

Features 1, 2, 3.

## Deliverables

- Updated tests (13+ files), regenerated baseline, updated docs
- Green full-suite + build proof

## Verification

Parent AC6 (documented seeded-draw changes), AC7, AC8.

```

    227|       (c: any) => c.family === 'business' || c.family === 'community-s…

 Test Files  5 failed | 292 passed (297)
      Tests  7 failed | 5449 passed | 8 skipped (5464)
```

## Root Cause

The failing assertion (`tests/main-street/move-to-hand-no-auto-select.test.ts:229`)
requires the seeded market (`setupMainStreetGame({ seed: 'no-auto-select-test' })`)
to contain **≥2 business/community-space cards**. The Main Street tier-rebalance
work (parent CG-0MT2WU0CX005Z143; commits incl. `b2bec26b` "Rebalance Main Street
tier synergy-type distribution (CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB)") changed card tiers / market
composition, which shifted the seeded draw so the market held only **1** such card
at that commit. The failure is a test-data coupling to seeded RNG, not a gameplay-logic
regression in the click-to-place flow (CG-0MSXIQIPJ000NDTL).

## Current Status (verified 2026-08-22 by plan skill)

- **Fixed on current dev** (`b2bec26b`): `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/move-to-hand-no-auto-select.test.ts` passes **8/8**.
- **Full suite green at current commit:** cached `npm --silent test` run (exit 0) at the exact current git state, ~16 min old (within 2h TTL).

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the failing commit: `git checkout a3b21ca7a103fe7bb9688360b97e70fb1ceadac2`
2. Run the failing test: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/move-to-hand-no-auto-select.test.ts`
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the
agent's current work item.

1. The test `tests/main-street/move-to-hand-no-auto-select.test.ts` passes when run against the latest `dev` (`npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/move-to-hand-no-auto-select.test.ts`).

3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`, plus `npm run build` quality gate).

## Implementation Notes

- The seeded-market coupling is the fragility: the test's `createMockScene()` builds the
  market from seed `'no-auto-select-test'` and assumes ≥2 business/community-space cards.
  Options: (a) verify-then-close — failure already resolved by the rebalance; or
  (b) defensive hardening — construct an explicit market in the test instead of relying on
  seeded composition, so future card-data changes cannot re-break this test.
- Follow test-failure triage runbook: `skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md`.

Browser tests: hand-first click flow for upgrades

**Priority: High** | **Type: Task** | **Parent: CG-0MT3IYSRL001VVUP**

## Problem statement

Browser tests to verify the upgrade hand-first click flow before implementation. These tests should initially fail (red) and pass after F-2 implementation (green).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Click a market upgrade card: moves to hand, consumes 1 action, card NOT auto-selected (pendingHandIndex null), uiPhase reverts to 'market'.
- Click the same-day moved upgrade in hand: sets pendingHandIndex, switches to 'placing-from-hand' state.
- Click an eligible street business: upgrade applies, pendingHandIndex resets, uiPhase returns to 'market'. Same-day composite does NOT consume additional action.
- Click a held (previous-day) upgrade in hand: sets pendingHandIndex, switches to 'placing-from-hand'. Clicking eligible business consumes 1 action.
- Click ineligible business: illegal-move feedback (shake), upgrade stays selected, player must click another target.
- Market upgrade cards show premium label and dim when action budget is spent.

## Key Files

# Intake Brief: Main Street: npm run monte-carlo (tsx) fails on ?raw CSV imports

## Headline

`npm run monte-carlo` fails with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` because tsx cannot load the Vite-style `card-data.csv?raw` import; switch the affected npm scripts from tsx to vite-node (the verified, in-repo-precedented runner) and update docs per the Doc-Update Policy.

## Problem statement

Three npm scripts that transitively import `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (`monte-carlo`, `monte-carlo-sweep`, `save-load-smoke`) fail under tsx with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` on `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`. tsx's loader misparses the Vite `?raw` query suffix for non-TS/TXT extensions, treating the CSV as a JS module. Root cause is in the import chain (`MainStreetCards.ts` line 18: `import cardDataRaw from './card-data.csv?raw'`), not in the harness logic — the same harness runs correctly under vite-node.

## Users

- **Developer running balance validation** — "I want `npm run monte-carlo` to just work so I can verify card balance after rebalancing card-data.csv." Example story: after editing `card-data.csv`, a developer runs `npm run monte-carlo` (or `monte-carlo-sweep`) and gets the JSON + CSV outputs described in docs.
- **Developer running the save/load smoke check** — "I want `npm run save-load-smoke` to pass so I can quickly verify persistence round-trips." Currently it crashes with the same loader error before running any scenario.
- **Producer/CI reader** — wants the documented commands in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` to remain accurate and working.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run monte-carlo` completes successfully end-to-end with the default settings (200 seeds, `mc-balance` prefix, greedy, maxTurns 25) and writes both JSON and CSV outputs; results are consistent with the verified working control run (200/200 runs; winRate 38.5%, medianScore 55.8, avgNoActionTurns 0 — i.e., determinism preserved, no balance drift).
2. `npm run monte-carlo-sweep` completes successfully in sweep mode (strategy × difficulty combinations) and writes its outputs.
3. `npm run save-load-smoke` completes successfully (exit 0, failures 0) — same root cause, same fix; expanded blast radius captured in this item.
4. Spot-check that unaffected tsx workflows still work (`npm run replay` or `balance-cards`) — no collateral regression from the runner switch.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, AGENTS.md scripts list, and docs/DEVELOPER.md, per the Doc-Update Policy; the vite-node rationale is documented in the same style as `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (line 67) for scripts importing `MainStreetCards.ts`.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` succeeds.

## Constraints

- The npm script **names and CLI flags must not change** (`npm run monte-carlo`, `--seeds/--seed-prefix/--maxTurns/--strategy/--out/--csv-out`, `--sweep`, etc.) — the harness CLI is a documented interface.
- Testing/validation criterion preserved: seeded determinism must be maintained (same seed → same deal order → same outputs; no reliance on RNG ordering changes).
- Prefer the established runner pattern over bespoke tooling: **vite-node** is the in-repo precedent for scripts that import `MainStreetCards.ts` (see `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`; `generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts` already uses it for exactly this reason) and is verified working for both broken entry points. A custom tsx loader hook for `?raw` would work but is more complex, repo-specific, and has no precedent — evaluated and rejected as the primary path.
- Doc-Update Policy applies (package.json scripts change).

## Existing state

- `package.json` lines 17–18, 21: `monte-carlo` / `monte-carlo-sweep` = `tsx scripts/monte-carlo.ts ...`; `save-load-smoke` = `tsx scripts/save-load-smoke.ts`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` line 18 imports `./card-data.csv?raw` (Vite bundler syntax, docs comment: "bundled at build time via Vite's `?raw`").
- Import chains that break under tsx: `scripts/monte-carlo.ts` → `MainStreetMonteCarlo` → `MainStreetState` → `MainStreetCards` → `?raw`; `scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` → `MainStreetState` → `MainStreetCards` → `?raw`.
- Reproduced failures: `npx tsx scripts/monte-carlo.ts` and `npx tsx scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` both exit 1 with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` (Node v22.22.1).
- Verified working: `node_modules/.bin/vite-node scripts/monte-carlo.ts --seeds 200 ...` (200/200; winRate 38.5%) and `node_modules/.bin/vite-node scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` (failures 0).
- Tests are unaffected — vitest handles `?raw` via Vite (e.g. `tests/main-street/tutorial-text-updates.test.ts`).
- Pre-existing: reproduced at commit b2bec26b (before CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA F1–F4) and at HEAD.

## Desired change

Switch `monte-carlo`, `monte-carlo-sweep`, and `save-load-smoke` package.json scripts from `tsx` to `vite-node` (entry scripts stay unchanged). Update docs per the Doc-Update Policy (AGENTS.md scripts list, docs/DEVELOPER.md; add the vite-node rationale for MainStreetCards-importing scripts in the same style as card-catalog.md). No engine or game code changes expected.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — scripts lines 17–18 (`monte-carlo`, `monte-carlo-sweep`) and 21 (`save-load-smoke`): tsx → vite-node.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — root cause location (`import cardDataRaw from './card-data.csv?raw'`); likely unchanged, but should be re-verified and its "bundled at build time" comment cross-referenced.
- `scripts/monte-carlo.ts`, `scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` — entry points; unchanged, but verification targets.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (lines ~197, ~230), `AGENTS.md` (scripts list, line ~76) — doc updates per Doc-Update Policy.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (line 67) — precedent/template for documenting the vite-node rationale.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT4RBCE2001DVCY — DUPLICATE** (status open): identical description, created 7 seconds earlier — a double-submit of this item. Producer to resolve (likely close in favour of this item, CG-0MT4RBHQR006C5GR).
- CG-0MT47FBLS000E7PW — "Monte Carlo sanity-check and full-suite verification" (open, in_progress): the discovering item; this bug was found while verifying it. `discovered-from` relationship already recorded.
- CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA — "Main Street: reputation score multiplier" (in_progress, plan_complete): commit b2bec26b predates this work; bug reproduced before and after it (pre-existing, not a regression of that item).
- CG-0MSAZL6O2008PTWY — "Replay CLI tests ... (spawnSync node --import tsx/esm ...)" (completed): related tsx CLI tooling context.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — documents the vite-node precedent for scripts importing `MainStreetCards.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (approach):** vite-node is the chosen fix over a tsx `?raw` loader hook — based on in-repo precedent (card-catalog.md), verified success on both broken scripts, and lower maintenance surface. If the producer prefers the loader-hook approach, scope is limited to the monte-carlo/save-load-smoke invocations and the doc updates shrink accordingly.
- **Assumption (scope):** fixing `save-load-smoke` in the same item is in-scope — same root cause, same fix, verified working under vite-node. If the producer wants to split it, create a child item.
- **Risk:** switching runners could subtly change module resolution for other `@alias` imports in the chain — mitigated by the verification ACs (output parity with the control run; full test suite) and by the existing precedent (vite-node already used for a MainStreetCards-importing generator).
- **Scope-creep guard:** no changes to harness logic, balance logic, or CSV handling are in scope; any balance-tuning opportunities surfaced by the working harness are separate work items (see CG-0MT47FBLS000E7PW).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Interview-driven questions were not required — the seed context (goal, confirmed working path, likely fix options) plus repo verification sufficed to draft the brief. Decisions recorded for auditability:

- Q: "Fix via vite-node or a custom tsx loader hook?" — Answer (research, no user input needed): **vite-node**. Evidence: `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` line 67 explicitly documents vite-node for `generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts` "(uses Vite-aware ESM loader because it imports deck-building functions from MainStreetCards.ts)" — the identical situation; both broken entry points verified green under vite-node. Loader-hook alternative has no precedent and higher maintenance; recorded as evaluated-and-rejected.
- Q: "Does the bug affect scripts beyond monte-carlo?" — Answer (repo verification): **yes — `npm run save-load-smoke` fails with the identical error** (transitively imports `MainStreetCards` via `MainStreetState`); verified green under vite-node. Included in ACs as in-scope via same-fix. `replay`, `export-transcripts`, `run-balance-cards` verified unaffected (no `?raw` chain).
- Q: "Duplicate work item CG-0MT4RBCE2001DVCY?" — Answer (evidence): identical description, created 7 s before this item, same discovered-from — a double-submit. Flagged to the producer for resolution; not blocking this intake.

# Banking mechanics — unit test suite

Test-first feature for **Main Street: action banking (bank unused actions for future turns)** (CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR). New `tests/main-street/action-banking.test.ts` covering every banking acceptance criterion; update existing AI/MC budget tests so they remain meaningful and correct under passive banking.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 · Banking on end-of-turn (test):** every unspent action in the day's budget banks — tests cover 0 / some / nearly-all actions taken (3 available, 1 taken → 2 banked); a fully-spent day banks 0.
- **AC2 · Cap enforced (test):** `bankedActions` never exceeds 2 in tests — further accumulation is discarded (end a day at cap with leftovers → stays 2); the bank cannot grow past the cap.
- **AC3 · Day-start composition (test):** tests assert day budget = 1 base + staff `actionsPerTurn` bonus + `bankedActions` capped 2 (banked 2 + GM → 4; banked 2 without GM → 3).
- **AC4 · Staff actions used first (test):** with General Manager employed (+1 `actionsPerTurn`), idle/partial days bank only the base 1 — the staff bonus never banks (idle GM day banks 1, not 2; GM day with 1 spent banks 1).
- **AC6 · State + persistence (test):** `bankedActions` round-trips save/load (legacy saves default to 0); undo/redo command snapshot/restore restores bank + `actionsRemaining` without double-banking.
- **AC7 · Quality gates (existing tests stay green):** updated `tests/main-street/ai-action-budget.test.ts` assertions are banking-aware (passive AI banks leftover actions, so later-day budgets exceed the old `maxPerDay <= 1` no-GM bound); `action-economy.test.ts` (full-budget-spend scenarios), `ai-strategy`, integration and Monte Carlo tests verified green.

## Minimal Implementation

- Mirror the patterns in `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts`: `setupMainStreetGame`, `executeDayStart(state, skipMarketRefill)`, `executeAction`, `processEndOfTurn`, `serializeMainStreetState`/`deserializeMainStreetState`, `gmTemplate()`.
- Use seeded setup for determinism; exercise banking across multi-day sequences (DayStart → spend → processEndOfTurn → DayStart again).
- Update `ai-action-budget.test.ts` budget assertions to assert banking-aware daily budgets (legit carry-over per the passive-AI rule; not arbitrary baselines).

## Dependencies

- None (TDD — written against intended behavior; may be authored alongside features 2–3 in the same worktree).

## Deliverables

- New test file + updated existing budget tests; all unit tests green.

# Engine — day-end banking + day-start composition

Third feature for **Main Street: action banking** (CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR): compute banking at day end in `processEndOfTurn` (single choke point shared by player and headless/AI paths) and compose banked actions into the day-start budget in `executeDayStart`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 · Banking on end-of-turn:** every unspent action in the day's budget banks via `bankedActions = min(2, bankedActions + min(actionsRemaining, 1))` computed in `processEndOfTurn` — 0 / some / nearly-all actions taken → remainder banks (3 available, 1 taken → 2 banked); fully-spent day banks 0.
- **AC2 · Cap enforced:** `bankedActions` never exceeds 2 as an engine invariant — further accumulation is discarded; the bank cannot grow past the cap.
- **AC3 · Day-start composition:** at DayStart, the day's budget is `1 base + staff actionsPerTurn bonus + bankedActions (capped 2)` implemented as `actionsRemaining = 1 + gmBonus + Math.min(2, state.bankedActions)` in `executeDayStart` (~L851); banked reserves are consumed as the player spends actions during the day (spending draws down the combined single-counter budget).
- **AC4 · Staff actions used first:** staff-derived actions (General Manager +1 `actionsPerTurn`) are consumed before the base/banked pool; staff bonuses themselves never bank — idle GM day banks exactly 1 (not 2); GM day with 1 spent banks 1; GM day with 2 spent banks 0.
- **AC4 · Both paths bank identically:** player path (`MainStreetTurnController.endTurn` → `processEndOfTurn`) and headless/AI path (`executeFullTurn` → `processEndOfTurn`) share the choke point; in-scope passive AI banks only on leftovers, never deliberately hoards.

## Minimal Implementation

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts`: banking computation in `processEndOfTurn` (before the day-end settle/turn increment); update the DayStart budget at ~L851 to `1 + gmBonus + Math.min(2, state.bankedActions)`.
- Clamp `bankedActions` ≥ 0 and ≤ 2 at the banking step.
- Run as part of `executeFullTurn` so headless/AI simulations exercise the same code path.

## Dependencies

- Feature 1 (tests), Feature 2 (state field exists).

## Deliverables

- Engine banking logic; feature 1 tests green against it.

# [test-failure] card-schema-validation.test.ts: runtime market/decks contain unregistered template IDs

## Headline

`CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` (the Main Street card template registry) omits the **staff** card family, yet staff cards are drawn into the runtime general market row. The schema-validation test therefore fails whenever a staff card lands in the market/decks at runtime.

## Problem statement

`tests/main-street/card-schema-validation.test.ts` asserts that every card ID present in the runtime game state (`state.market.cards`, `state.incidentDeck`, `state.decks.business/event/upgrade`) maps — after stripping the `-\d+` instance suffix — to a registered template ID in `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` (from `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts`). The assertion fails (reproduced at HEAD, seed `schema-registry-validation`) because the runtime market contains a staff card (`staff-lookout-0` in the failing deal) and staff templates are never registered: `rebuildTemplateArrays()` adds business, community-space, event, and upgrade templates to `_CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES`, but staff templates are built into `_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES` only.

Since the staff-in-general-market work (CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55), `refillSingleRowMarket` draws staff cards into the single-row market alongside the other four families — so staff cards are legitimate runtime cards whose template IDs must be registered. This is a registry gap (a bug), not a broken test: the schema registry should cover every family that can appear in the runtime market/decks.

## Users

- **Developers extending the Main Street card pool** — they rely on `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` (via `card-schema-validation.test.ts`) as the guardrail that every runtime card corresponds to a known template. Today the guardrail errors on valid staff cards.
- **Players** — an unregistered template can surface as a missing name/title in animation lookups (`CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES.get(templateId) ?? cardId` in `MainStreetAnimator.ts` falls back to the raw card ID, e.g. showing `staff-lookout-0` instead of "Lookout").

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All staff template IDs present in `card-data.csv` (family `staff`) are registered in `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` so that every staff card ID valid at runtime (e.g. `staff-lookout-0`) resolves to a registered template ID.
2. `tests/main-street/card-schema-validation.test.ts` passes: `runtime market/decks only contain registered template IDs` and `all template IDs are represented in CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` both green against `dev` with the reproduction seed.
3. The validation test covers the full set of runtime card families — the runtime sample includes staff (market/decks) so this regression cannot silently recur; consider also asserting `state.decks.staff` (and `decks.communitySpace`) explicitly rather than only via market draw.
4. Runtime CSV reload (`loadTemplatesFromCsv` / `resetTemplatesToDefault` → `rebuildTemplateArrays`) keeps the registry consistent — staff re-registered/cleared together with the other families.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (regenerating any doc/card-catalog artifacts required by the change).
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix should be surgical: register staff templates in `rebuildTemplateArrays()`; do not weaken the validation test.
- Staff cards in the general market row is intended behavior (CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55) — the fix must not remove staff from the market.
- `CARD_TIER_MAP` already includes staff rows (every CSV row with a non-empty `tier`), so the staff tier entries exist; only the name registry is missing them.
- Static staff SVGs exist under `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/` (9 files) and `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.loadCardSvgSources()` iterates `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES.keys()` — registering staff will also make the SVG loader pick up the existing static staff assets, which is consistent (verify no duplicate/stale texture keys).

## Existing state

- `rebuildTemplateArrays()` (MainStreetCards.ts ~L92–212) registers `bizTemplates`, `csTemplates`, `evtTemplates`, `upgTemplates` into `_CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` but builds `_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES` from `staffRows` without touching the name map.
- `createStaffDeck()` builds runtime staff card IDs as `` `${template.id}-${c}` `` — same instance-suffix convention as other families, so `.replace(/-\d+$/, '')` correctly recovers the template ID.
- Reproduced at HEAD (87934225): market contains `staff-lookout-0`, and `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES.has('staff-lookout') === false`.
- Sibling test-failure item CG-0MT4ZR4AP006MCUC (`MainStreetIntegration.test.ts` save/load migration old-format saves) also stems from the staff-card migration work but is a separate failing assertion (`restored.decks.staff` vs `staffCardMarket` handling) — related, not a duplicate.

## Desired change

Add staff templates to `_CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` inside `rebuildTemplateArrays()` (e.g. a loop over the freshly built `_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES` or over `staffRows`), so the name registry covers all five runtime families bidirectionally with load/reset, and optionally extend the test's runtime sample to explicitly include `state.decks.staff` / `decks.communitySpace` for full-family coverage.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — `rebuildTemplateArrays()`: register staff templates in `_CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES`; `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` export.
- `tests/main-street/card-schema-validation.test.ts` — failing test; extend runtime coverage to staff (and community-space) decks.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — iterates `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES.keys()` for SVG fetch; verify staff asset pickup after registration.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES.get(templateId) ?? cardId` title lookup benefits from staff registration.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (and any generated card catalog) — update if the doc lists registered families or staff.

## Related work

- CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55 — "State, Serialization & Refill: staff in the general market" (in_progress, parent epic CG-0MT2WTN0L004JA53) — the change that introduced staff into the general market row; root-cause precursor.
- CG-0MT4ZR4AP006MCUC — sibling test-failure from the same CI run (MainStreetIntegration save/load migration); related, distinct assertion.
- CG-0MT3KZOBZ005IRYE / CG-0MT3KZOUX007GQ44 / CG-0MT3KZPDR004IEIH — staff purchase/render/test work items under the same "staff in general market" epic.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: None asked — the failure signature plus direct repo reproduction (staff card `staff-lookout-0` in the runtime market with `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES.has('staff-lookout') === false`) fully determined the root cause; the obvious fix (register staff templates) was validated against registry usage sites (SVG loader, animator title lookup, tier map) and requires no user decision. Source: repo investigation (runs of the failing test at HEAD, diagnostic vitest run, `wl` lookups for CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55 / CG-0MT4ZR4AP006MCUC).
